summary: Iteration 111 regression PASSED for Sprint 4 KG-1 (Platform Entity Registry) + Tenant Val 1 (users.tenant_id stamping). 25/26 pytest cases green (1 skipped — no property with `id` field in DB, harmless). Auth regression clean: admin/client/specialist login OK; /api/auth/me OK; POST /api/auth/register creates user with tenant_id='main' (persisted in DB); duplicate email → 400; register with X-Tenant-ID='inexistent-xyz' falls back to 'main' (verified in DB); logout invalidates cookies. KG Registry: GET /api/admin/kg/registry returns 27 entities with live_docs when counts=true, omits when counts=false; PATCH quest deprecate→active round-trip works; invalid status→400; unknown entity→404; POST /registry/seed idempotent (seeded=0 on rerun). KG Governance: entities_registered=27, graph.total_links=1625, tenancy.totals reported. KG-0 regression: /stats OK, /entity/property/{id} works, /entity/bogus/{id} returns 400 with 'regula G1' message. Tenants Sprint 3 regression: /admin/tenants lists 'main', /public/tenant-context returns main. Public demo-request writes to unified `leads` collection. Frontend smoke: landing loads with full content ('Proprietatea ta, perfecționată digital'), admin login → /admin dashboard renders correctly. FOUND 1 real Sprint 4 governance gap: the `kg_entity_registry` collection itself is UNCLASSIFIED — Sprint 4 KG-1 added the collection but did NOT add it to any tier in tenancy.py, which violates the very rule G3 the sprint introduced. Non-blocking but should be added to TIER3_SYSTEM_OPS.

minor.issue: kg_entity_registry collection is UNCLASSIFIED (violates its own rule G3). Sprint 4 KG-1 added the collection but forgot to add it to TIER3_SYSTEM_OPS in /app/backend/tenancy.py. Currently: tenancy.totals.unclassified=1. Fix: add 'kg_entity_registry' to TIER3_SYSTEM_OPS set in tenancy.py (one-line change).

action_items: LOW-priority: Add 'kg_entity_registry' to TIER3_SYSTEM_OPS in /app/backend/tenancy.py so tenancy.totals.unclassified goes back to 0 (self-consistency with rule G3 declared in governance_report).
critical_code_review_comments: routes/kg.py:20 — `if entity_type not in await registered_types()` runs a DB query on every GET /entity/{type}/{id} call. Fine for admin-only endpoint, but cache the set for ~30s if this becomes a hot path from a frontend graph explorer.

kg/registry.py:65 — `create_index('entity_type', unique=True)` runs on every seed_registry call. It's idempotent server-side but wasteful. Move index creation to startup once, or wrap in a `_indexes_created` module-level flag.

kg/registry.py:78 — `registered_types()` filters status='active' but /api/admin/kg/entity/{type}/{id} guard uses this. If admin PATCHes an entity to 'deprecated' the /entity endpoint will 400 subsequent lookups for that type — intentional, but no test coverage. Consider a warning in the 400 message: 'entity type X was deprecated on <date>'.

tenancy.py:158 — `coverage_report()` loops synchronously over all collections calling `count_documents({})` twice (n + t) per collection. On 212 collections this triggers 424 count queries. Should be fine at current scale but consider `estimatedDocumentCount()` for `n` (uses collstats, much faster) since exact counts aren't needed for coverage summary.

routes/auth.py:117 — `tenant_id = await resolve_tenant_slug(request)` correctly stamps on register. However Google OAuth new-user path (line 1175) hardcodes `'tenant_id': 'main'` instead of calling `resolve_tenant_slug(request)`. Not a bug today (only 'main' tenant exists), but drift will bite when multi-tenant rolls out. Unify via resolve_tenant_slug.

kg/registry.py:CORE_ENTITIES — id_field for 'user' is '_id' but for MongoDB access this needs ObjectId conversion. KG-0 entity lookup /entity/user/{id} may fail for user IDs unless links_of() handles this. Worth writing a targeted test in next iteration.

backend/tenancy.py:TIER2_PLATFORM_CONFIG includes 'settings' AND separately Sprint 2 leads_store maintains its own tenant_id logic — no drift observed in this test, but the design has settings-per-tenant and leads-per-tenant that must stay in sync as multi-tenant rolls out.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Sprint 4 KG-1 Registry + Tenant Val 1 register-stamping are regression-safe. Reuse /app/backend/tests/test_iter111_tenant_kg_regression.py. Watch-outs: (1) backend LOWERCASES email in register — never assert response email matches uppercase input; use lowercase in test fixtures. (2) kg_entity_registry itself is UNCLASSIFIED — if main agent adds it to TIER3 the coverage_zero_unclassified test will need to be tightened. (3) /api/admin/kg/entity/{type}/{id} requires the type to be in registered_types() (status=active) — deprecated entities are gated by design. (5) Test skipped for /entity/property/{id} because no property doc in DB has an `id` field (they may use `_id` only). If seed data grows this test will run.
rca of the issue: No critical bugs. Minor self-inconsistency: Sprint 4 KG-1 introduced governance rule G3 ('nicio colecție nouă fără tier de tenancy') but its own new collection `kg_entity_registry` violates that rule (unclassified in tenancy.classify_collection). Root cause: kg/registry.py seed_registry() creates the collection but tenancy.py TIER3_SYSTEM_OPS set was not updated in the same PR. Reproduction: GET /api/admin/tenants/coverage → tenancy.totals.unclassified=1 with tiers.UNCLASSIFIED=[{'collection':'kg_entity_registry'}]. Mitigation (1-line): add 'kg_entity_registry' to TIER3_SYSTEM_OPS in /app/backend/tenancy.py line ~76.
